value.rationale: Fault-tolerant metric bases are a natural minimum-redundancy landmark problem. The classical nonisomorphic strongly regular (16,6,2,2) pair has identical numerical optimum size six but sharply different connectivity under landmark relocation: total rigidity vs connectivity at single replacement, repaired by a provably sharp two-site batch on Shrikhande. Exact base counts, symmetry and distance profiles supply meaningful structural information not determined by the strong regular parameters or general metric dimension.
